review: Independent core adversarial review before normalized-search-cache optimization
verdict: Accepted for the explicitly limited first private milestone after two ownership blockers were fixed
artifact_identity_note: The sha256 section records the exact artifact used for this review's executed ownership probes. The final_handoff section records the subsequent complete rebuild verified by the integrating parent.

findings.before: A correctly rehashed manifest with producer nested 110 levels passed native parsing, registered a reader handle, then failed Ruby JSON parsing at depth 101. No Reader finalizer owned the handle; closing unreturned handle 1 afterward returned true.
findings.fix: Native requests, manifests and facts enforce a 64-level structural bound; manifest producer/diagnostics shapes are checked before registration. Ruby response parsing explicitly allows 128 levels for envelope headroom.
findings.after: The hostile manifest raises Thistle::LimitExceeded before registration. The next valid native open receives handle 1.

findings.before: Four real Thread#kill interruptions during Reader.new over a 4000-method snapshot left four registered, unreturned native handles even after GC.start. Thread.handle_interrupt(Exception => :never) did not fix termination.
findings.fix: Reader acquisition and finalizer attachment defer Object interrupts; an outer ensure closes acquired handles when construction does not complete. Cleanup and explicit close use the same interruption protection.
findings.after: All four uninstrumented acquisitions were interrupted and all four handles were released. A deterministic real Thread#kill at the native-return handoff also leaves no retained handle before or after GC.

negative_control.description: The original pre-review constructor is loaded only into disposable probe processes. Both ownership tests detect the genuinely acquired handle leak.

review_observations: The C bridge copies Ruby input before releasing the GVL and frees owned input/response buffers through rb_ensure.
Arc ownership pins an already-started native query when its reader is concurrently closed.
Store access is descriptor relative, refuses symlinks/nonregular files and checks bounded reads.
Publication validates before changing CURRENT; already-fixed post-selection directory sync errors explicitly report commit_uncertain.
Source expansion and Check verify captured byte digests and source-coordinate agreement.
The registry's serialized-data/handle budgets are honestly documented as distinct from a heap or process RSS cap.
remaining_qualifications: This review is for a private milestone, not broad platform, launch-parity or production-security certification.
Prism is C code invoked through Rust bindings. The bounded-stack worker and exercised parser probes do not establish hostile-input safety or replace process isolation, external deadlines and fuzzing.
Decoded allocations, concurrent in-flight operations and process RSS do not have a measured aggregate hard cap.
Power-loss recovery, retention, disk quotas, generalized fork support and public platform distribution remain separately qualified launch work.
A complete store author can produce another internally consistent store; content digests are integrity checks, not authenticity or authorization.
